questions.question: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake. It connects to the ____ valves.
questions.correctAnswerText: Relay
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves. These valves help apply trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Supply air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: To safely couple a trailer, follow the correct steps. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: While inspecting the coupling under the trailer, you should:

options.text: Detach the jaws from around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the "emergency" position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: Look into the back of the fifth wheel. Check that the fifth wheel jaws grip the kingpin shank properly.

questions.question: In a sudden turn, the ____ trailer is most likely to roll over.
questions.correctAnswerText: Last
questions.explanation: Turn gently and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous. The last trailer is most likely to roll over.

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away:

options.text: The trailer will not have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will not have brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers lack spring brakes. If air leaks from the tank, the brakes will not work. The wheels will spin freely.

questions.question: If air pressure is lost in the emergency line, it will:

options.text: The tractor protection valve to open.
The rear trailer to detach from the combination.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency brakes to activate.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. When air pressure is lost in the emergency line, the emergency trailer brakes will activate.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, the ____ trailer should be directly behind the cab.
questions.correctAnswerText: Heaviest
questions.explanation: Position the heaviest-loaded trailer closest to the tractor. Place the lightest trailer in the rear.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), apply the brakes:

options.text: In the same way as a vehicle without ABS.
As the vehicle is placed in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the same way as a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: With ABS, brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: An automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops to:
questions.correctAnswerText: 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops the flow of air.

questions.question: Proper coupling technique:

options.text: Is the same on all vehicles.
Is essential to the safe operation of a vehicle.
Includes ensuring that the fifth wheel plate is not greased.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is essential to the safe operation of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Learning proper coupling and uncoupling is vital to safe operation of combination vehicles. Improper coupling is dangerous.

questions.question: What does a shut-off valve do?

options.text: It is on the front of a trailer.
It is on the instrument panel.
It stops air from leaving the brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops air from leaving the brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve must stay closed to prevent air from leaving the brakes.

questions.question: When crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for you.
Wait for a large enough gap to cross safely.
Use only your mirrors to check.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large enough gap to cross safely.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other vehicles. Always wait for a safe gap in traffic before crossing.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If stuck on railroad tracks, get out of your vehicle right away and walk away from the tracks. Then call emergency help.

questions.question: If your trailer goes off course while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Pull forward, readjust, and back up again.
Get out and move the trailer into position.
Turn the steering wheel all the way left until the trailer straightens out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward, readjust, and back up again.
questions.explanation: If your trailer goes off course while backing, pull forward to reposition your vehicle before backing up again.

questions.question: When does an automatic tractor protection valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out if air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: Which trailer is most likely to roll over in a quick turn?
questions.correctAnswerText: Last
questions.explanation: Turn gently and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous and can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: After coupling, how much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.correctAnswerText: No space
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: How does a fully-loaded rig compare to an empty rig for rollover risk?

options.text: Just as likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity from the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?

options.text: It supplies the trailer with air.

questions.correctAnswerText: It supplies the trailer with air.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: How should you load cargo to reduce rollover risk?

options.text: Load it as far forward as possible.
Load it as far back as possible.
Load it as low as possible.
Stack it as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load it as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Load cargo as close to the ground as possible to reduce rollover risk. Also take curves and corners slowly.
